deep.reconstruction:
This page holds no mathematical derivation. It is a sheet of raw numerical readings in pencil, almost certainly instrument readings from a physical experiment, with one short note.

(a) Top left: two values, 1.9(?) and 1.9, then a horizontal rule.

(b) Left column: about 41 readings scattered tightly around 8.0. They run 8.4, 8.1, 8.0, 8.1, 8.0, ..., with values of 7.8 to 8.1 thereafter. Short horizontal strokes split the column into groups (near 7.9/7.8 and after 8.1). Grouping like this is typical when one averages blocks of successive readings.

(c) Second column: about 19 readings, also around 7.9 to 8.0, again with a dividing stroke. The '11,8' is almost certainly a misreading or slip for 7.8. The '17,9' (written over '1') is 7.9.

(d) Third column, headed 'Lad. oben' (perhaps 'Ladung oben' or a position label such as 'upper'):
- First series: 95.2, 95.2, 95.1, 95.2, 95.15, 95.(struck, possibly .17), 95.1, 95.1, 95.1, 95.1, 95.1, 95.0. That is 12 readings.
- Below a rule comes '95,126'. This is evidently the arithmetic mean of the block. My check: with the struck entry read as 95.17, the mean is 95 + 1.52/12 = 95.1267. With 95.15 it is 95.125. Either way it is about 95.126.
- Second series after a second rule: 96.4, 96.3, 96.3, 96.2, 96.1, 96.1, 96.1, 96.0, 95.9, 95.8, 95.8, 95.8, 95.7, 95.7, 95.7, 95.6, 95.7, 95.6. This is a slow, monotone drift downward of about 0.8 scale units. It looks like a scale reading relaxing toward equilibrium, or a slowly decaying charge or deflection.

(e) Fourth column: numbered readings 1) 8.0, 2) 8.0, 3) 8.0, ..., 12) 8.0, then 7.9, 8.0, 7.9, 8.0, 7.9.

(f) Note to the right of the mean: 'Genauer beträgt diese Correction ...' ('More precisely this correction amounts to ...'). The rest is partly struck and illegible. It indicates that the mean was used to compute an instrumental correction, such as a zero point or rest position.

The context is the next page, which lists deviations +1, 0, -1, -2, ... against an index 1 to 210. That is an oscillating or drifting sequence of small integer deviations. Together the pages look like laboratory or observational data, plausibly connected with Weber's Göttingen measurement practice (mirror-and-scale readings), in which Riemann participated around 1853–54.

The only computation on the page is the averaging of readings (the 95.126 mean) and, implicitly, a correction derived from it. No formulas appear.
errors: Mean '95,126' is consistent with the 12 readings only if the struck entry is about 95.16–95.17. With 95.15 the exact mean is 95.125; with 95.2 it is 95.129. So it is either a correct mean with an uncertain entry or a minor rounding difference. It is not a substantive error.
The '11,8' in the second column is out of range for the series (7.8–8.1). It is surely 7.8, either a misreading or a pen slip.

With the struck entry read as 95.15 the mean is 95.125.
Total drift of the second 95/96 series is 0.8 scale units.
